## What's inside

<table>
<tr>
<td width="33%" valign="top">

**Extensions and browsing**
- Runs CloudStream `.cs3` extensions unchanged
- Add repositories by URL or shortcode
- Home, Continue Watching and search across all your sources
- Details with cast, trailers, seasons and episodes

</td>
<td width="33%" valign="top">

**Player**
- HLS, MP4 and WebM in the app, with [mpv](https://mpv.io) for the rest
- Multiple sources, quality and audio tracks
- Subtitles with size, style and delay controls
- Skip intro, next episode and picture-in-picture

</td>
<td width="33%" valign="top">

**Library and downloads**
- Watch lists, history and episode progress
- Direct and HLS downloads you can pause and resume
- Choose your own downloads folder
- No ads, no tracking, no account

</td>
</tr>
</table>

## Install

<details open>
<summary><b>Windows</b></summary>

1. Download the `Setup.exe` file.
2. Open it. If a blue "Windows protected your PC" screen appears, click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This appears because the app isn't code-signed.
3. Follow the installer. It doesn't need admin rights.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>macOS</b></summary>

1. Download the `.dmg` for your Mac. To check which one you have, open the Apple menu and choose **About This Mac**: a **Chip** line means Apple Silicon, and a **Processor** line means Intel.
2. Open it and drag **CloudStream Desktop** into **Applications**.
3. Open the app. If macOS blocks it, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

If macOS says the app is damaged, run this in Terminal and open it again:

```bash
xattr -cr "/Applications/CloudStream Desktop.app"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Linux</b></summary>

Download the file for your system, then run the matching command from the folder it's in:

```bash
# Ubuntu, Debian, Linux Mint
sudo apt install ./CloudStream*.deb

# Fedora, RHEL
sudo dnf install ./CloudStream*.rpm
```

If videos don't play, install the video codecs. On Ubuntu and Debian:

```bash
sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav
```

</details>

## Get started

1. **Add a repository.** Open **Settings → Extensions**, click **Add repository**, and paste a repository URL or shortcode. [Here's where to find one](https://github.com/ahasan-ullah/cloud_stream_pc#cloudstream-repositories).
2. **Install extensions.** Click the repository, then click the download icon next to each extension you want.
3. **Start watching.** Go to **Home**, open a title and click **Play**.

The [full guide](https://github.com/ahasan-ullah/cloud_stream_pc#how-to-use-it) covers search, downloads, backups and more.

> [!CAUTION]
> Extensions are code that runs on your computer, and they are not sandboxed. Only add repositories you trust.

## Good to know

- Windows is the tested platform. The macOS and Linux versions are new, so please [open an issue](https://github.com/ahasan-ullah/cloud_stream_pc/issues) if something doesn't work.
- Some extensions depend on Android-only features and can't run on a computer. Your other extensions keep working.
- The built-in player handles MP4, WebM and HLS. For MKV, HEVC and DASH, install [mpv](https://mpv.io/installation/).

## Thank you, CloudStream

**A huge thank you to the [CloudStream team and contributors](https://github.com/recloudstream/cloudstream/graphs/contributors).** This app runs their library and extractors, loads the extensions built for their app, and takes its design from CloudStream. If you enjoy it, please [star the original project](https://github.com/recloudstream/cloudstream) and support them.
